primary_claim: A minimal from-scratch Mamba (state-space model) implementation trained on modular addition exhibits grokking (generalizing after overfitting), and tensor (Canonical Polyadic) decomposition of the gating-activation tensor across epochs, tokens, and gate units reveals interpretable factors that track the train-test loss gap and separate representations by the parity of the input sum, in contrast to standard 2D PCA of the gate activations, which showed no clearly interpretable structure.
contradicts_or_qualifies: PCA-based decomposition of gating activations was not interpretable, in contrast to tensor (Canonical Polyadic) decomposition of the full 3D activation tensor, which did yield factors interpretable in terms of learning/grokking dynamics and input parity
stated_future_work: Investigate how these results can be leveraged for intervening on learning, e.g. designing gate perturbations to make activities more coherent and potentially speed up learning
Test whether grokking happens in SSMs trained on other tasks
Test whether tensor decomposition (or similar methods) can be useful in larger models
limitations_stated: Epistemic status: approximately 20 hours of side-project work using only a Colab notebook

The minimal Mamba implementation significantly simplifies the original architecture (single state-update step, single convolution, single residual connection, no stacked blocks), so results may not transfer to full-scale Mamba models
quote: This non-transformer-based model can also exhibit grokking (i.e., the model learns to generalise after overfitting to the training data).
